events.whyItMatters: InMode is now the target of a contested take-private: activist holder Steel Partners' $16.75/share all-cash offer (a 20% premium to the unaffected price) tops the CEO-led group's $16.20 bid and lets public holders roll up to 40% into the private company. The board's independent directors must respond by July 13, so the near-term catalyst is whether a bidding war develops or the CEO group prevails.

phases.headline: Steel Partners offers to acquire InMode for $16.75 per share in cash
Haifa court blocks InMode board from deciding between competing buyout bids pending Steel Partners injunction hearing, extends response deadline to July 19
Steel Partners Urges InMode Shareholders to Vote AGAINST the Re-Election of Dr. Hadar Ron and AGAINST Extraordinary Special Committee Compensation at the July 30 Annual General Meeting

events.whyItMatters: After three rejections Prologis has a firm Rule 2.7 recommended offer on the table: 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each Segro share, valuing Segro at roughly GBP14.3bn (~$18.8bn) with a partial cash alternative capped at GBP3.5bn -- up to about 1054p a share, a 42% premium to the June 23 unaffected close. It would take one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs off the LSE and hand Prologis a European logistics platform, but the consideration is mostly paper, so Segro holders end up owning Prologis stock, and completion is not expected until the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Prologis pushes for SEGRO engagement on potential combination
Segro board unanimously rejects Prologis's unsolicited ~886p/share takeover proposal as inadequate
UK's Segro rejects Prologis' $18.2 billion sweetened takeover proposal
Prologis tables 'best and final' £14bn ($18.8bn) takeover proposal for Segro; Segro board signals it is minded to recommend as both sides secure PUSU deadline extension to August 12
Prologis Announces Recommended Acquisition of SEGRO plc
phases.priceReaction: 42% premium to the June 23 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: A 12-state antitrust coalition led by California's AG is suing to block Paramount Skydance's ~$110bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger and seeking a court order to halt closing — even though the deal is already signed and was DOJ-cleared in June 2026, a state-level legal challenge to theatrical and cable-distribution concentration adds a real risk of delay or an unwound deal.

phases.headline: Coalition of 12 states sues to block Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. Discovery merger
Writers Guild of America sues to block Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, alleging the deal will suppress writers' wages and cut job opportunities
Paramount Skydance's $110B merger with Warner Bros. Discovery paused by judge

Paramount Skydance agrees to joint stipulation pausing $111bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger until five days after an antitrust trial or June 1, 2027, whichever is earlier; WGA's preliminary-injunction motion withdrawn as moot

Paramount agrees to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders roughly $7 million per day if the merger remains unclosed after September 30, 2026, as part of the litigation-pause stipulation -- a potential ~$1.7bn cost if the pause runs to the June 1, 2027 outside date
Paramount, Warner Bros. merger challenges set for a 12-day antitrust trial starting March 2, 2027 before US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin in Oakland
UK Competition and Markets Authority approves Paramount Skydance Corporation acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery at Phase 1, taking the deal's clearances to 66 jurisdictions

events.whyItMatters: EQT's revised A$2.6bn (A$22.07/share, ~22% premium) approach for Perpetual — raised twice in a week, and just two weeks after the board rejected an earlier A$2.45bn bid — keeps the storied Australian wealth/asset manager in a live takeover process; it's the firm's fourth takeover approach since 2022, and the board has still not committed to engage.

phases.headline: Australia's Perpetual Snubs $1.69 Billion Takeover Offer From EQT Over Valuation
EQT Sweetens Pursuit of Australia's Perpetual With $1.75 Billion Bid
EQT Raises Perpetual Takeover Bid to A$22.07 a Share (~A$2.6bn) After Board Rejects A$21.64 Approach
Perpetual Limited Board Rejects EQT AB's A$22.07 Per Share Takeover Proposal
EQT raises takeover offer for Australian wealth manager Perpetual to A$22.50 a share (~A$2.65bn), up from the A$22.07 proposal the board rejected
Perpetual rejects EQT's A$22.50-a-share (~A$2.6bn) proposal as not in shareholders' best interests, but offers limited non-public information and says it will engage on an improved offer

events.whyItMatters: Frasers Group, already Hugo Boss's largest shareholder at ~26.6%, has launched a formal, regulator-approved EUR38/share tender for the rest of the company; Hugo Boss's own board says the price undervalues the business and is urging shareholders to reject it, so the outcome of a contested control fight at a major European fashion house now hinges on the acceptance period running to July 27.

phases.headline: Hugo Boss pops 8% after top shareholder Frasers launches $2 billion takeover offer
Hugo Boss board rejects Frasers Group bid, urges shareholders not to accept
Frasers Group crosses 30% stake threshold in Hugo Boss, triggering mandatory-offer rules under German takeover law; confirms EUR38/share is its final price

Frasers Group's EUR38-per-share offer for Hugo Boss becomes unconditional after European Commission merger clearance; the initial acceptance period closed July 27 and an additional acceptance period runs to August 13

events.whyItMatters: AMD locks in a marquee AI-chip customer and financial backer in one deal — Anthropic commits to buy tens of billions of dollars of AMD Instinct MI450 chips (up to 2GW of deployment) while AMD invests up to $5bn in Anthropic's equity, cementing AMD as a credible second sourcing option to Nvidia inside one of the largest frontier AI labs.

phases.headline: AMD to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic as part of computing power deal

events.whyItMatters: Repligen's ~$1.5bn purchase of BioLife Solutions adds market-leading CryoStor biopreservation media to its bioprocessing tools, deepening its exposure to the fast-growing cell and gene therapy manufacturing chain — a bolt-on funded mostly in stock (64%) rather than cash.

phases.headline: Repligen to Acquire BioLife Solutions, Expanding Its Cell Therapy Capabilities with Market Leading Biopreservation Media

events.whyItMatters: Iberdrola's ~$2.3bn purchase of an 80% stake in Caruna, Finland's largest electricity distributor, extends its regulated-networks push into a Nordic market seeing surging grid demand from data centers and electrification -- roughly two-thirds of Iberdrola's 2025-2028 capex is earmarked for distribution networks like this one.

phases.headline: Iberdrola Agrees to Buy 80% Stake in Caruna Group for EUR2 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Combining Norway's two mid-cap North Sea producers creates Europe's largest independent oil and gas company and targets $250-300m of 2027-2032 synergies from shared financing and overhead -- though Eni's ~57% post-deal stake means the combined firm stays majority-controlled by Var Energi's parent rather than becoming fully independent.

phases.headline: Var Energi to Buy BlueNord for $1.3 Billion, Creating Europe's Biggest Independent Oil and Gas Producer

events.whyItMatters: CD&R-owned OCS's 46.8%-premium all-cash offer removes UK facilities-management leader Mitie from public markets entirely, consolidating two of the sector's largest players (combined ~GBP8.5bn revenue, 84,000+ staff) just as demand for AI-driven data-center facilities services accelerates.

phases.headline: OCS Group Agrees GBP3.1 Billion ($4.17bn) Takeover of Mitie Group, Delisting It From the London Stock Exchange

events.whyItMatters: Dassault buys a life-sciences regulatory and safety-data platform to fuse with its existing 3DExperience biotech tools, aiming to link molecule, patient and real-world-outcome data on one AI platform -- deepening its push into pharma software beyond its core CAD/PLM base.

phases.headline: Dassault Systemes to Acquire ArisGlobal, Creating a Unified AI Intelligence Platform for the Life Sciences Industry

events.whyItMatters: Ford brings in a Chinese EV/hybrid partner to fill an underused European plant and co-develop four new models (including a new Bronco-family member) -- a rare case of a Detroit automaker directly partnering with a Chinese rival on home-market EV production rather than competing purely on cost.

phases.headline: Ford and Geely Auto Establish Joint Venture in Spain for Localized Production at Ford's Valencia Plant

events.whyItMatters: Mapfre's $1.54bn ($105/share cash, ~44% premium) all-cash purchase takes Safety Insurance Group private, closing out its run as an independent public insurer and giving Mapfre a bigger vehicle for US expansion, pending Massachusetts regulator and HSR clearance with close expected Q1 2027.

phases.headline: Mapfre to Acquire Safety Insurance Group for $1.54 Billion in All-Cash Deal

events.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's $1.5bn multiyear prepayment locks in dedicated US 2.5D/3D advanced-packaging and test capacity at Amkor, giving Amkor a marquee anchor customer for its domestic expansion while helping Nvidia diversify AI-chip packaging supply onshore through 2028.

phases.headline: Amkor Technology Announces Strategic Partnership with NVIDIA to Expand Advanced Packaging and Test for Next-Generation AI Infrastructure

events.whyItMatters: Verizon's $1bn dark-fiber supply deal with Google gives it a new physical-infrastructure revenue line tied directly to hyperscaler AI data-center buildout, positioning the telco as a connectivity landlord to the AI capex cycle rather than just a wireless/broadband carrier.

phases.headline: Verizon signs $1 billion dark fiber deal with Google for AI data centers

events.whyItMatters: Alphabet raises its 2026 capex guide from $180-190bn to as much as $195-205bn, telling investors AI infrastructure demand keeps outpacing build-out -- the market read the increase as a margin risk despite a cloud beat, sending shares down after-hours.

phases.headline: Google Boosts 2026 Spending Estimate to as Much as $205 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Popular raises its quarterly dividend 20% (to $0.90/share) and authorizes up to $1bn in new buybacks, a meaningful step-up in capital return relative to its size that signals confidence in the Puerto Rico-based bank's capital position.

phases.headline: Popular Announces Increased Quarterly Dividend and New $1 Billion Share Repurchase Program

events.whyItMatters: Albertsons collapses 11 operating divisions into 4 under its new 'ACI Edge' plan targeting $200m of run-rate savings by FY2027, alongside a CFO departure and a cut full-year EPS guide (to $1.75-1.85 from $2.22-2.32) -- a genuine restructuring of the operating model, not just a soft quarter.

phases.headline: Albertsons cuts fiscal 2026 sales and profit outlook, unveils 'ACI Edge' restructuring plan

events.whyItMatters: A 5-year, ~$200bn MOU locks in Samsung's HBM4/HBM4E memory supply and 2nm-and-below foundry capacity for Broadcom's AI accelerators -- a major foundry-customer win against TSMC and a long-run revenue floor for Samsung's contract-manufacturing and memory businesses.

phases.headline: Samsung and Broadcom sign $200 billion chip deal spanning memory, foundry and packaging

events.whyItMatters: SK Telecom will build a 2GW NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI factory while SK hynix -- roughly 60% of the global HBM market -- enters a long-term supply and co-development pact with NVIDIA, locking in the dominant AI-chipmaker's memory pipeline and giving SK hynix a large multi-year revenue commitment tied to next-gen HBM.

phases.headline: SK Group and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership Across AI Factories and Next-Generation Memory

events.whyItMatters: Samsung SDS commits to a large-scale Claude Enterprise rollout across roughly 70,000 employees and 20 Samsung affiliates, giving Anthropic a marquee enterprise deployment inside one of Asia's biggest conglomerates and signaling Samsung is diversifying its AI stack beyond OpenAI.

phases.headline: Samsung SDS Forges Alliance with Anthropic, Expanding AI Partnerships Beyond OpenAI

events.whyItMatters: Bank of America raises its quarterly dividend 14% (to $0.32/share), a double-digit capital-return step-up that signals management confidence in the bank's post-stress-test capital position.

phases.headline: Bank of America declares quarterly dividend of $0.32 per share, up from $0.28

events.whyItMatters: Microchip buys Israeli edge-AI/vision chipmaker Hailo, reportedly at a steep discount to its prior ~$1bn valuation, adding AI-accelerator IP to its portfolio even though management says the deal isn't financially material on its own -- a build-out of its AI roadmap via distressed-asset M&A.

phases.headline: Microchip Technology Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Hailo

events.whyItMatters: WSP Global raises its unsolicited bid for Dutch engineering consultancy Arcadis to EUR51.50/share (from a rejected EUR48.50) in roughly half cash, half stock -- the second approach in a live, escalating takeover situation for a ~EUR7.5bn asset, with Arcadis's board yet to respond to the sweetened offer.

phases.headline: Arcadis Confirms Takeover Bid From WSP, Shares Surge on Revised Offer
Arcadis unanimously rejects second unsolicited proposal from WSP Global Inc

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia would guarantee roughly $250bn of lease and debt financing so OpenAI can take a 10GW, SoftBank-developed Ohio campus, with a separate ~$350bn chip-purchase financing line under discussion on top. It would lock in years of demand for Nvidia silicon, but turns the chipmaker into a balance-sheet backstop for its own largest customer -- concentrating credit risk that did not previously sit on Nvidia's books. Talks are early-stage and could collapse.

phases.headline: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion financing for data center, WSJ reports

events.whyItMatters: argenx pays $2.2bn in cash ($77/share, ~86% premium to Forte's VWAP since its July 9 vitiligo data) entirely from cash on hand and with no financing condition, buying a first-in-class anti-CD122 antibody (FB102) with clinical proof-of-concept in two autoimmune indications -- a move to broaden its pipeline beyond the FcRn franchise that currently carries the company.

phases.headline: argenx to Acquire Forte Biosciences, Inc., Adding First-in-Class anti-CD122 Antibody, FB102, to its Immunology Pipeline

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia takes a multibillion-dollar equity stake (reported at ~$5bn) in Ilya Sutskever's pre-revenue, pre-product AI lab and supplies next-generation Vera Rubin capacity to raise SSI's compute by an order of magnitude -- another instance of Nvidia funding the customers that buy its chips, which grows the order book while concentrating vendor-financing risk on its own balance sheet.

phases.headline: Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence Inc. and NVIDIA Announce Long-Term Strategic Partnership

events.whyItMatters: Orange contributes five French data centres to a 50-50 venture with infrastructure investor Morrison backed by a EUR3bn investment programme targeting 400MW -- roughly ten times Orange's current data-centre capacity, turning an underused telco asset base into a sovereign-AI hosting business funded largely with partner equity and debt rather than Orange's own balance sheet.

phases.headline: Orange and Morrison announce plans to create a data centre joint venture to strengthen Europe's digital sovereignty

events.whyItMatters: Expand Energy pays $1.25bn from cash and its revolver for gas marketer Twin Eagle, lifting marketed volumes to ~14 Bcf/d and raising its incremental marketing free-cash-flow target 50% to $750m a year -- a shift from pure-play producer toward an integrated gas business whose earnings depend on basis and logistics rather than the wellhead price alone.

phases.headline: Expand Energy Corporation to Acquire Twin Eagle, Creating North America's Leading Integrated Natural Gas Company

events.whyItMatters: Sazerac's revived $32/share all-cash approach (~$15bn, a 23% premium) is its second run at Brown-Forman this year, and this time it went over the board's head directly to shareholders while offering to improve terms if the board engages -- putting a family-controlled spirits franchise into a public pressure campaign it has so far refused to negotiate under.

phases.headline: Brown-Forman Says It Rejected Sazerac's Unsolicited Takeover Bid

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia takes about 4.5% of Naver through a ~$1bn new-share issue -- making the chipmaker Naver's third-largest shareholder behind the National Pension Service and BlackRock -- while Brookfield funds up to $9bn of a $10bn AI factory that lifts the GAK Sejong data centre from 55MW to 200MW by 2028. Naver gets sovereign-AI scale without carrying the capex alone; Nvidia gets another equity-linked customer locked into Blackwell and Vera Rubin.

phases.headline: Nvidia to invest $1 bil. in Naver for 4.5% stake, with Brookfield backing a $10 billion AI factory build at the GAK Sejong data centre

events.whyItMatters: A Blackstone-Brookfield-KKR consortium takes 49% of Kuwait Oil Company's 320km crude pipeline network under a 20.5-year lease-and-leaseback ('Project Peregrine'), handing KOC $7.85bn upfront against a $16bn headline value while it keeps 51% -- one of the largest Middle East infrastructure privatisations yet, and a large, long-duration, contracted asset for three listed alternative managers hunting scale in infrastructure.

phases.headline: Kuwait Oil Company Signs US$16.0 Billion Infrastructure Partnership Involving Its Crude Oil Pipeline Network With a Consortium Comprising Blackstone, Brookfield and KKR

events.whyItMatters: TransDigm pays ~$1.066bn cash for precision engineered-materials maker Prince & Izant, bought from Industrial Growth Partners -- its largest bolt-on of the year and a continuation of the debt-funded, high-margin proprietary-parts roll-up the whole TransDigm equity story rests on.

phases.headline: TransDigm Group Announces Agreement to Acquire Prince & Izant for Approximately $1.066 Billion in Cash

events.whyItMatters: Leonardo DRS pays $450m cash for Raft, a McLean, Virginia open-architecture mission-software firm, buying into multi-domain data fusion and AI rather than building it -- a step up the stack from hardware-centric defence electronics, funded from cash and the revolver, accretive to adjusted EPS in year one and carrying a ~$50m present-value tax benefit.

phases.headline: Leonardo DRS to Acquire Raft, Expanding Multi-Domain AI, Data Fusion and Mission Software Capabilities

events.whyItMatters: Grant Thornton's $5bn all-cash purchase of CBIZ at $55/share -- a ~54% premium to the 30-day VWAP, backed by fresh New Mountain Capital equity -- takes the largest publicly traded US accounting and advisory firm private and creates the fifth-largest US professional services provider, the sector's biggest combination in more than 25 years. A go-shop period running to August 27 leaves the door open to a topping bid.

phases.headline: Grant Thornton Advisors to Acquire CBIZ for $5 Billion in Transaction Supported by New Mountain Capital
phases.priceReaction: +17.7% intraday, biggest single-day gain in over 20 years

events.whyItMatters: CMS Energy will exit non-utility renewables development and sell NorthStar Clean Energy's non-Michigan assets, keeping only Michigan facilities such as Dearborn Industrial Generation -- a board-approved shift toward a near pure-play regulated utility that cuts parent-level funding needs by more than $500m through 2030 and redirects that capital into rate-based investment.

phases.headline: CMS Energy Announces Second Quarter Results, Strategic Decision on NorthStar Clean Energy Services, Introduces Guidance for 2027

events.whyItMatters: Boston Scientific's board-approved global restructuring commits $700-800m of pre-tax charges through 2029 to strip out roughly $500m of annual costs via supply-chain consolidation, production-line transfers between plants and headcount reductions -- a margin-defence program at a company that has grown mainly by acquisition, and a signal that cost discipline, not just growth, now drives the plan.

phases.headline: Boston Scientific unveils new restructuring plan, expects job cuts

events.whyItMatters: ICE pays $167/share in cash (~$5.7bn enterprise value, a 33% premium) to buy MarketAxess, folding the largest institutional electronic corporate-bond network into its own retail bond franchise and fixed-income data business -- a bet that the $145trn bond market is the next asset class to electronify, funded with cash and new debt behind a $6.25bn bridge facility and targeting only ~$100m of cost synergies, so the case rests on revenue and network effects rather than cuts.

phases.headline: ICE to buy MarketAxess in $5.7 billion deal to expand fixed-income offerings

events.whyItMatters: Lloyds raises its interim dividend 30% to 1.58p and adds a GBP1bn buyback -- GBP1.9bn of first-half distributions -- while setting out an 'Accelerate 2030' plan targeting ~20% return on tangible equity, a sub-45% cost-income ratio and 225bps+ of annual capital generation by 2030 -- turning a 17.1% first-half RoTE and a 13.1% pro forma CET1 ratio into a committed multi-year capital-return trajectory rather than a one-off payout.

phases.headline: Lloyds launches GBP1bn buyback and new 2030 plan after beating profit forecasts

events.whyItMatters: NXP is in talks to buy Ambarella, whose low-power edge-AI vision silicon would slot into an automotive franchise already worth roughly half of NXP's ~$15.1bn 2026 revenue -- buying software-defined-vehicle, radar and camera capability rather than building it. The FT report puts the price above $3bn but stresses talks are ongoing and may not produce a deal, so the premium is not yet fixed and rival bidders could still surface.

phases.headline: NXP in talks to buy chip developer Ambarella, FT reports

events.whyItMatters: KKR's $127-a-share, ~$5.7bn all-cash take-private of medical-device contract manufacturer Integer Holdings is now signed and unanimously recommended by the board, resolving the strategic review opened in April 2026 at a 51.8% premium to the unaffected price and a 28.8% premium to the 30-day VWAP. The question shifts from whether a deal happens to whether shareholder and regulatory approvals land by the targeted year-end close -- or whether a topping bid surfaces first.

phases.headline: KKR nearing deal to acquire Integer Holdings, WSJ reports
Integer to Be Acquired by KKR in Transaction Valued at Approximately $5.7 Billion
phases.priceReaction: 51.8% premium to the April 29 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Vodafone pays GBP4.3bn from existing cash for CK Hutchison's 49% of VodafoneThree, taking sole ownership of the UK's largest mobile operator just over a year after the CMA-cleared merger completed. Full control lets it move faster on the GBP11bn network investment plan and the GBP700m of annual cost and capex savings targeted by FY30 -- at the cost of spending the cash up front and carrying 100% of the integration risk.

phases.headline: Vodafone takes full ownership of VodafoneThree

events.whyItMatters: Amazon lifts 2026 cash capex guidance to roughly $220bn from ~$200bn, blaming higher memory costs, with Jassy saying AI capacity stays constrained through 2027 and declining to detail how the extra $20bn is funded. It lands alongside AWS growth accelerating to 37% and a $496bn backlog -- the second hyperscaler in ten days, after Alphabet, to tell investors AI infrastructure demand is outrunning the build-out plan.

phases.headline: Amazon hikes 2026 capex to $220 billion due to higher memory costs
phases.priceReaction: shares surged the following session on Q2 results

events.whyItMatters: The Wall Street Journal reports Tesla executives were told to prepare for a separation of the China business -- spin-off, sale or closure -- to clear the national-security path for a merger with defence contractor SpaceX. Gigafactory Shanghai is Tesla's largest plant, with over 950,000 units of annual capacity and historically more than half of global deliveries, so a separation would be the biggest structural change in the company's history. Elon Musk called the report 'absurdly fake news' and Tesla China called it false information, so this is a contested single-source report, not an agreed plan.

phases.headline: Tesla weighs sale of China business to pave way for potential SpaceX merger, WSJ reports

events.whyItMatters: Everus pays $295m in cash -- funded from cash on hand and its credit facilities -- for a 25-year-old maker of modular mechanical and electrical building infrastructure serving data centers, advanced manufacturing and healthcare. Epsilon expects roughly $250m of 2026 revenue at a low-double-digit EBITDA margin, so this buys off-site prefabrication capacity and a data-center-exposed revenue stream rather than building them, with closing expected in Q3 2026.

phases.headline: Everus to Acquire Epsilon Industries, Premier Off-Site Modular Construction Solutions Provider

events.whyItMatters: SG Fleet Topco -- the Pacific Equity Partners vehicle that took SG Fleet private -- has put an unsolicited, non-binding A$3.60-a-share (~A$760.3m) scheme proposal to FleetPartners, a 27% premium that would put two of Australia's largest fleet-management and novated-leasing books under one private owner. The board has committed to nothing and is evaluating with UBS and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, so the open questions are whether it engages at all and whether a combination of this scale clears the ACCC.

phases.headline: Australia's FleetPartners shares on track for best day in 6 years on $534 million takeover bid

events.whyItMatters: Doosan pays KRW2.3trn (~$1.6bn) for 70.6% of SK Siltron, Korea's only dedicated silicon-wafer maker and the world's number three in 12-inch wafers -- its largest deal since Bobcat and a pivot out of heavy industry into semiconductor materials, with a stated ambition to lift SK Siltron revenue to about KRW3trn by 2031. For SK Inc. it is a major balance-sheet disposal of a core affiliate; completion is scheduled for January 2027.

phases.headline: SK sells control of wafer maker SK Siltron to Doosan for W2.3tr

events.whyItMatters: Holcim is exiting the Philippines outright -- 68% of its local business goes to China's Huaxin Cement for $527m now, the balance over three to five years for at least $280m, roughly $807m in total -- its largest divestment since the $1bn sale of its Nigeria arm to the same buyer. It continues the redeployment of capital out of emerging-market cement and into higher-multiple building solutions, with completion expected in the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Holcim to sell Philippines unit to China's Huaxin in $807 million deal

events.whyItMatters: The UK Takeover Panel pushed Castlelake's put-up-or-shut-up deadline out to August 7 to match Apollo's, so both bidders for easyJet must now declare a firm offer or walk away on the same day. easyJet's board has an agreement in principle with Apollo at 715p a share (~GBP5.7bn) and is no longer minded to recommend Castlelake's 690p, which makes Friday binary: either a GBP5.7bn take-private of Europe's second-largest low-cost carrier goes firm, or a two-bidder auction collapses back to a standalone airline.

phases.headline: UK Takeover Panel extends Castlelake's deadline for a firm easyJet offer from August 3 to August 7, aligning it with Apollo's deadline
Apollo agrees to buy UK airline EasyJet in $7.7 billion deal as Castlelake withdraws
phases.priceReaction: 81% premium to the GBP3.94 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Prysmian pays $95 a share in cash (~$3.8bn enterprise value, a 30% premium to Atkore's July 31 close) to buy a US maker of electrical conduit, cable management and metal framing -- the step that turns the world's largest cable manufacturer into a broader electrical-solutions supplier into North American data centres and grid build-out. It targets $150m of annual synergies by 2029 and earnings accretion from year one, and it ends the strategic review Atkore opened in September 2025 at a ~57% premium to the pre-review price.

phases.headline: Prysmian Strikes Deal to Buy US Electrical Maker Atkore for $95.00 per Share in Cash

events.whyItMatters: Supernus and Indivior combine in a tax-free all-stock merger of equals -- 1.5401 Indivior shares per Supernus share, leaving Indivior holders with ~56.5% and Supernus holders ~43.5% of a ~$2.2bn-revenue CNS biopharma listed on Nasdaq as SUPN -- with $125m of expected annual cost synergies and a $1bn pre-closing special cash dividend to Indivior investors part-funded by a $650m Citibank term loan. It is a scale answer to both companies' single-franchise concentration risk, but the debt-funded special dividend means the combined balance sheet starts levered.

phases.headline: Supernus Pharmaceuticals and Indivior Pharmaceuticals to Merge, Creating a Diversified CNS Biopharmaceutical Leader with Significant Scale

events.counterparty: Public Investment Fund (with Silver Lake, Affinity Partners)
events.whyItMatters: The largest leveraged buyout on record closes: EA leaves the Nasdaq after 37 years at $210 a share in cash (a 25% premium to its $168.32 unaffected price), funded with ~$36bn of equity and ~$20bn of JPMorgan-committed debt, leaving Saudi Arabia's PIF with 93.4%, Silver Lake 5.5% and Affinity Partners 1.1%. It removes a $55bn name from public markets, sets a new ceiling for what sponsor-plus-sovereign capital can take private, and puts a major Western games publisher under majority state ownership.

phases.headline: Electronic Arts completes $55 billion take-private by PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the largest leveraged buyout ever

events.whyItMatters: IonQ closes its ~$1.8bn purchase of semiconductor foundry SkyWater Technology after the FTC cleared it without conditions, over the chairman's push to impose fair-access commitments to rival quantum firms that hold SkyWater contracts. It makes IonQ a vertically integrated quantum company that owns its own fab rather than renting capacity -- and hands it control of a chokepoint several competitors depend on.

phases.headline: IonQ closes $1.8bn SkyWater acquisition after US FTC clearance

events.whyItMatters: Resideo completes the spin-off of ADI Global Distribution, distributing one ADI share for every two Resideo shares to holders of record on July 20 and listing ADI on the NYSE as ADIG from August 4. It splits the company into a products business and a distribution business that investors can now value separately -- removing the conglomerate discount, but also removing ADI's revenue scale from the Resideo that remains.

phases.headline: Resideo completes spin-off of ADI Global Distribution; ADI to begin trading on the NYSE as 'ADIG' on August 4

events.whyItMatters: Curium's up-to-$8bn purchase of Lantheus combines two of the largest radiopharmaceutical businesses and takes Lantheus off the Nasdaq, but only $102.50 a share is cash at closing -- the remaining $12.00 sits in non-transferable CVRs tied to prostate-cancer and neurology diagnostic and DEFINITY sales milestones through 2030, so holders reach the headline $114.50 only if the combined franchise delivers. Closing is not expected until the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Curium Announces Definitive Agreement to Merge with Lantheus

events.whyItMatters: Procter & Gamble pays $3.8bn in cash for science-backed supplements maker Thorne, its biggest push yet into the vitamins, minerals and supplements market and a bolt-on to a health portfolio that already includes New Chapter, Metamucil and Align. It also hands seller L Catterton a return of more than $3bn on the roughly $680m it paid in 2023 -- a reminder that P&G is buying at the top of a wellness cycle rather than early into one. Closing is expected later in 2026, subject to regulatory clearance.

phases.headline: Procter & Gamble will acquire supplements brand Thorne for $3.8 billion, CEO tells CNBC

events.whyItMatters: Both shareholder bases have now approved the all-stock merger of equals between Axalta and AkzoNobel -- 0.6539 AkzoNobel shares per Axalta share, leaving AkzoNobel holders with ~55% and Axalta holders ~45% of a coatings group with ~$17bn of revenue, ~$3.3bn of adjusted EBITDA and $600m of targeted pre-tax run-rate synergies (90% inside three years). The vote removes the shareholder-approval risk that had hung over the deal since the governance terms were revised on July 23; what remains is regulatory clearance and a EUR2.5bn pre-completion distribution condition, with closing guided to late 2026 or early 2027.

phases.headline: Axalta Shareholders Approve Proposed Merger of Equals with AkzoNobel

events.whyItMatters: SpaceX and NVIDIA will jointly design the compute payload for the Starmind AI1 satellite -- NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs running datacenter-class AI workloads in low Earth orbit -- and Musk used SpaceX's first post-IPO earnings call to say SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure exclusively on NVIDIA going forward, against an eventual ambition of up to a million satellites. It gives NVIDIA an exclusive lock on a brand-new compute frontier and a customer with its own launch capacity, and it closes off SpaceX as a market for rival accelerators; AMD fell on the same news.

phases.headline: SpaceX Commits Exclusively to Nvidia, Unveils Starmind: AMD Falls 9% on Record Quarter

events.whyItMatters: A five-year patent cross-license ends every pending Netlist-Samsung dispute and converts a litigation lottery ticket into contracted cash: $239m upfront (net of Korean withholding tax) plus quarterly fees of up to $32.9m across twenty quarters, up to ~$897m gross in total. It also comes with a supply agreement letting Netlist buy up to $300m of Samsung DRAM and NAND a year (up to $1.5bn over the term) and a 10m-share equity purchase by Samsung under a five-year lock-up. For a company whose equity story was previously a binary bet on court outcomes, that is a different business.

phases.headline: Netlist, Samsung Reach Multi-Million Dollar Memory Tech Deal
phases.priceReaction: +46.5% to $3.75, biggest one-day gain in five years

events.whyItMatters: The largest pharma combination ever floated -- a roughly $400bn AstraZeneca/Bristol Myers Squibb merger reported by the FT and Bloomberg as exploratory -- has been flatly denied by a senior source close to the matter, who told Reuters there never was a deal to be done and no discussions are under way. Neither company has commented on the record either way, so the practical read is that the premium the market briefly priced into BMY and the 7% discount it applied to AZN both rested on a combination that is not being pursued; the antitrust overlap in oncology that made it hard remains the reason it stays unlikely.

phases.headline: AstraZeneca in talks with Bristol Myers Squibb on $400 billion megadeal, FT reports
No deal between AstraZeneca and BMS, senior source insists: "There is no deal between AstraZeneca and BMS. There never was a deal to be done, and there are no discussions between the companies"

events.whyItMatters: Nielsen pays $13.60 a share in cash -- roughly $2.15bn of enterprise value, a 30% premium to DoubleVerify's 60-day VWAP -- to take the ad-verification firm private and bolt media-quality measurement onto its own audience-measurement franchise, targeting a combined business with more than $4bn of annual revenue. It removes one of the few remaining listed pure-play ad-tech names from the Nasdaq and hands a private-equity-owned Nielsen an end-to-end measurement stack, but it is funded with committed debt from Barclays, BofA and Citi plus incremental equity, so the combined entity starts levered. Closing is not expected until the first quarter of 2027.

phases.headline: Nielsen to Acquire DoubleVerify, Creating a Leading, Independent Media Intelligence Platform

events.whyItMatters: Deutsche Telekom more than doubles its 2026 buyback envelope from EUR2bn to as much as EUR5bn and lifts full-year free cash flow guidance to around EUR20bn after a core-earnings beat -- management explicitly framing the increase as a response to the shares' depressed valuation rather than a routine top-up. For a DAX heavyweight that has historically prioritised deleveraging and dividends, committing an extra EUR3bn to repurchases is a genuine shift in how the cash gets returned.

phases.headline: Deutsche Telekom Raises 2026 Share Buyback By Up to EUR3 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Williams buys all of Momentum Midstream for up to $5.5bn -- about $3.5bn of cash and debt plus roughly $2bn of Williams equity, at an implied ~8.5x 2027 EBITDA -- adding more than 4,000 miles of Haynesville gathering pipe, over 1m dedicated acres and three take-or-pay pipelines that move gas toward Gulf Coast LNG and power demand. Paired with the $1.5bn Delta Access project and the Shelby Trough Connector, it is a large, part-equity-funded bet that Haynesville-to-Gulf takeaway is where the LNG and data-center load actually shows up.

phases.headline: Williams Delivers Strong Second-Quarter 2026 Results; Announces Strategic Acquisition of Momentum Midstream Connecting Haynesville to Gulf Coast LNG and Power Demand

events.whyItMatters: Diamondback's board doubles the share-repurchase authorization to $16bn from $8bn, leaving ~$9.9bn available, alongside raised 2026 guidance of 522+ MBO/d of oil and 1,000+ MBOE/d total after crossing the million-barrel-equivalent mark. Doubling the buyback rather than the dividend or the drilling budget is a statement that management sees its own equity as the best use of Permian free cash flow at current strip prices.

phases.headline: Diamondback Energy, Inc. Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results; Board doubles share repurchase authorization to $16.0 billion

events.whyItMatters: Driven Brands' board unanimously rejects an unsolicited $18.00-a-share all-cash proposal from activist holder ADW Capital -- a 41% premium to the $12.74 close and 42% to the 30-day VWAP -- calling it highly conditional and without a credible basis to proceed. ADW's stated thesis is that the 4,200-location car-wash and auto-services group is cheap because of self-inflicted structural, capital-allocation and governance failures, so the rejection converts a valuation argument into a public pressure campaign that now hangs over the shares whether or not financing ever materialises.

phases.headline: Driven Brands Holdings Inc. Rejects Non-Binding, Highly Conditional and Unsolicited Proposal from ADW Capital

events.whyItMatters: Dream Finders pays $33.50 a share in cash -- about $915m of equity and roughly $2.2bn of enterprise value including assumed debt -- for Beazer Homes, creating the sixth-largest US homebuilder at around 13,000 annual closings and adding Indianapolis, Las Vegas, Sacramento, southern California and Delaware to its map. It ends a months-long pursuit that began with a private offer in February and several rejections, and targets more than $100m of annual run-rate cost synergies. The bet is that scale beats caution: this is debt-assisted consolidation placed into a soft housing market, with closing guided to Q4 2026 subject to Beazer shareholder and regulatory approval.

phases.headline: Dream Finders Homes to Acquire Beazer Homes, Creating Sixth-Largest U.S. Homebuilder

events.whyItMatters: Kirin pays C$45.75 a share in cash for Jamieson Wellness -- about C$2.0bn of fully diluted equity and C$2.5bn of enterprise value, a 27% premium to the 20-day and 32% to the 60-day VWAP to June 24 -- taking the top-share brand in Canada's vitamins, minerals and supplements market off the TSX and giving the Japanese brewer a full-scale North American health platform rather than a beachhead. It is the second large supplements deal in under a week after P&G's $3.8bn purchase of Thorne, which says more about where consumer-staples capital is going than about either buyer. Closing is guided to Q4 2026, subject to a September shareholder vote plus court and regulatory approvals.

phases.headline: Jamieson Wellness Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Kirin in C$2.5 Billion Transaction
phases.priceReaction: 27% premium to the 20-day VWAP to June 24

events.counterparty: Oaktree Capital Management, SFS Group Capital (Ishbia family)
events.whyItMatters: UWM raises $2.05bn of permanent capital from Oaktree and the Ishbia family's new SFS Group Capital vehicle -- 1.5m Series A-1 and 150,000 Series A-2 preferred shares at a $1,000 stated value paying 10% in cash or 13% accreted, plus 330m warrants -- and suspends its common dividend to repay debt and MSR financing facilities, with a $400m rights offering held in reserve. It lands alongside a $451.9m second-quarter loss, equity nearly halved to $985.3m and non-funding leverage more than tripled to 6.13x, so this is a balance-sheet rescue with heavy dilution attached rather than an opportunistic raise. The market read it that way: the shares fell about 35%.

phases.headline: UWM Holdings Corporation Announces $2.05 Billion Strategic Capital Partnership with the Ishbia Family and Oaktree

events.whyItMatters: Thyssenkrupp shareholders approved, with 99.99% of votes at an extraordinary general meeting, the spin-off of 49% of tk accelis -- the materials trading arm with roughly 15,500 staff and about EUR11.4bn of sales, its largest division by revenue and valued near EUR3.6bn by Jefferies -- clearing the way for a separate Frankfurt listing as soon as end-October with Thyssenkrupp retaining majority control. It is the third carve-out under the ACES 2030 plan after hydrogen and defence, converting the conglomerate into a holding company and giving investors a directly priceable distribution business; the steel division, where a spin-off or IPO is still only being explored, remains the unresolved piece.

phases.headline: Thyssenkrupp owners approve materials spinoff in latest restructuring move

events.whyItMatters: Delaware's Court of Chancery has invalidated Verisk's December termination of its $2.35bn purchase of roofing-software provider AccuLynx, finding that Verisk's own willful conduct caused the closing condition to fail, ordering it to attempt to complete the deal and entitling AccuLynx to recover its direct costs plus interest. It revives an acquisition Verisk wrote off more than seven months ago and puts a specific-performance obligation back on the buyer -- but the court compelled effort, not an outcome: completion still depends on an FTC review that has never finished.

phases.headline: Delaware judge orders Verisk to proceed with $2.35 billion AccuLynx deal

events.whyItMatters: Diageo commits $1.2bn of restructuring spend to take out roughly $1bn of annual cost -- $850m from a new operating framework landing across fiscal 2027 and 2028, plus $150m from supply-chain work -- after organic net sales fell 2% on weakness in North America and Asia Pacific. Fiscal 2026 already absorbed $0.9bn of restructuring charges, so this is a funded rebuild of the operating model by a new CEO rather than a cost-discipline gesture, and investors treated the savings plan, not the results, as the news.

phases.headline: Diageo unveils $1.2bn restructuring plan as sales decline hits North America and Asia Pacific
phases.priceReaction: shares surged as the $1bn cost-saving plan outweighed weaker annual results

events.whyItMatters: CVC's up-to-915p-a-share cash proposal values Bodycote at about GBP1.56bn and puts the FTSE 250's dominant thermal-processing specialist -- an asset-heavy franchise serving aerospace, autos and energy with no listed pure-play peer -- into a live two-sponsor auction decided by a single penny. The board has said it would recommend either proposal and has opened confirmatory due diligence to both, so the open question for holders is no longer whether Bodycote leaves the LSE but which sponsor firms up by the 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline.

phases.headline: Bodycote confirms a possible cash offer from CVC Advisers of up to 915p a share (907.8p cash plus a 7.2p permitted interim dividend), valuing it at ~GBP1.56bn, and grants confirmatory due diligence ahead of a 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline

events.whyItMatters: Veritas Capital's up-to-914p-a-share proposal sits one penny below CVC's for the same GBP1.56bn asset, which is what makes this a genuine auction rather than a single-bidder approach: Bodycote's board is running both parties through confirmatory due diligence separately and on an expedited basis, and either bid would be recommended. For Veritas the prize is the largest independent heat-treatment and specialist-technology network in the West; for holders, the 1p spread means the outcome turns on which sponsor moves first before 2 September rather than on price alone.

phases.headline: Bodycote confirms a competing possible cash offer from Veritas Capital of up to 914p a share (906.8p cash plus a 7.2p permitted interim dividend), with the board prepared to recommend either proposal

events.whyItMatters: ContextLogic is completing its conversion from the wound-down Wish marketplace into a holding company that parks cash-generative industrials behind a large tax-loss shield: gChem is its second operating business after US Salt. The $850m cash price is funded partly by a $650m rights offering at the public-company level, fully backstopped at $9.00 a unit by a consortium led by Abrams Capital and BC Partners, so existing holders either write a cheque or watch the sponsors' ownership concentrate. Management guides the combined businesses to roughly $95-105m of free cash flow in 2027.

phases.headline: ContextLogic to Acquire gChem for $850 Million, funded in part by a $650m rights offering fully backstopped at $9.00 per unit by a consortium led by Abrams Capital and BC Partners

events.whyItMatters: ENEOS is buying scale in US petrochemicals rather than shrinking alongside Japanese domestic fuel demand: TPC is North America's largest independent C4 hydrocarbon processor and the region's butadiene share leader, and the ~$1.3bn enterprise value brings Houston petrochemical operations plus terminals at Port Neches, Texas and Lake Charles, Louisiana. The deal lifts the ENEOS Group to the world's third-largest butadiene capacity and moves refining cash flow into a feedstock-advantaged Gulf Coast platform, with closing targeted for October 2026.

phases.headline: TPC Group to Be Acquired by ENEOS Holdings at approximately $1.3bn enterprise value, giving the ENEOS Group the world's third-largest butadiene production capacity

events.whyItMatters: Bernhard Capital pays $43.00 a share in cash -- about $1.0bn of enterprise value and a 58% premium to Bowman's unaffected August 7 close -- to take the engineering and infrastructure consultancy off the Nasdaq, backed by $605m of committed BCP equity and $550m of committed debt across term loan, revolver and delayed-draw facilities. It is the second listed engineering consultancy put in play inside a fortnight after WSP's rejected approaches for Arcadis, and the go-shop running to September 13 leaves the door open to a topping bid before the Q4 2026/Q1 2027 close.

phases.headline: Bowman Consulting Group Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Bernhard Capital Partners for $43.00 Per Share in Cash
phases.priceReaction: 58% premium to the August 7 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Blackstone Infrastructure's Safe Harbor pays $53.00 a share in cash -- roughly $1.5bn of enterprise value and a 96% premium to MarineMax's January 30 unaffected close, 110% to the 90-day VWAP -- ending a six-month process that began with an unsolicited approach. It takes the largest listed US recreational-boating retailer private at a weak point in the marine cycle and hands Safe Harbor 65 marinas and storage sites plus 70 dealerships, its biggest deal since Blackstone bought it for $5.7bn in 2025. The offer is not financing-contingent, so what remains is shareholder and regulatory approval before the targeted end-2026 close.

phases.headline: MarineMax Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Blackstone Infrastructure Portfolio Company, Safe Harbor, in a $1.5 Billion All-Cash Transaction
phases.priceReaction: 96% premium to the January 30 unaffected close; shares surged on the report

events.whyItMatters: Teledyne pays $18.90 a share in cash -- about $1.1bn including Varex's net debt and equity awards, at roughly an 88% premium -- for the largest independent maker of X-ray tubes and flat-panel detectors. It moves Teledyne from imaging sensors into the medical-imaging component supply chain and removes one of the few listed pure-play suppliers of next-generation CT detectors from the market. Closing is targeted for early 2027.

phases.headline: Teledyne to Acquire Varex Imaging Corporation

events.whyItMatters: Archer buys Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid entirely in stock -- Boeing receives newly issued shares equal to 19.75% of Archer's pre-closing count, about 16.5% after closing, plus a board nominee -- absorbing its main autonomous-eVTOL rival and picking up in Insitu a defence drone business with more than $200m of annual revenue. For a pre-revenue eVTOL developer that converts dilution into an operating defence franchise and Boeing as an anchor holder; for Boeing it is another non-core disposal that costs no cash while keeping access to Wisk's autonomy stack through a separate collaboration. Closing is expected by end-2026, subject to antitrust review.

phases.headline: Archer to Shape Physical AI Future of Aerospace and Defense with Acquisition of Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid Subsidiaries; Boeing to Invest in Archer and Collaborate

events.whyItMatters: Intel's $15bn underwritten common-stock offering -- its first public share sale since listing in 1971, with a $2.25bn underwriter option on top -- funds capital expenditure management has already guided up to about $20bn for 2026 and 'meaningfully' higher in 2027. Choosing equity over debt protects the balance sheet and the investment-grade rating, but it places the cost of the AI and foundry build-out on existing holders through dilution rather than on lenders, and the market read it that way.

phases.headline: Intel Announces Proposed $15 Billion Common Stock Offering

events.whyItMatters: Bloomberg reports Ryan Cohen is weighing pulling GameStop's $56bn unsolicited bid for eBay -- rejected in May as 'neither credible nor attractive' -- in favour of a partnership or joint venture that would put eBay's trading-card and collectibles business into GameStop's roughly 1,600 US stores, with GameStop seeking a board seat off the back of the stake it already owns. GameStop is down about 28% and eBay up 7.6% since the proposal surfaced, so the arithmetic that made the bid arguable has gone; no decision has been made and this is sourced reporting, not an announcement.

phases.headline: GameStop's Ryan Cohen Weighs Pulling $56 Billion EBay Offer

events.whyItMatters: Tabcorp agrees to buy wagering-technology supplier BetMakers at A$0.24 a share (~A$283m) by scheme of arrangement, unanimously recommended by the BetMakers board, six months after informal talks between the two collapsed in February. It brings in-house the platform Tabcorp needs to modernise its own wagering stack plus an international B2B business, and targets A$30m of annual cost savings by the end of year two -- material for a company of Tabcorp's size. Completion is guided to the third quarter of Tabcorp's FY2027, subject to BetMakers shareholder, court, ACCC and gaming-regulator approvals.

phases.headline: Tabcorp to acquire BetMakers in A$283 million deal, unanimously recommended by the BetMakers board
